title: Targeted warmup and speculative kernel-swap with KV quiet-locks
author: Marina Ortega
description:
Motivation: In production traffic we see transient latency spikes and occasional correctness mismatches during aggressive kernel swaps and KV-cache reconstructions. This PR introduces a targeted warmup stage and a speculative kernel-swap path that can be rolled back quickly when correctness or latency signals deviate from SLOs. Additionally we implement a 'quiet-lock' mode for KV operations to reduce contention during warmup and swap windows. The goal is to improve 99th-percentile latency and reduce user-visible regeneration errors while retaining most of the throughput gains from faster kernels.

What changed (single-line checklist): - Add targeted warmup controller that warms only affected tensor shards rather than full-model passes; warmup uses short synthetic batches derived from sampled traffic. - Implement speculative_kernel_swap operator in runtime/kernel_selector to switch kernels optimistically and keep a lightweight verification probe that validates the first few outputs against the incumbent kernel. - Add KV quiet-locks: an adaptive backoff + lightweight lock that prevents noisy concurrent reconstructs while allowing read progress for active requests. - Expose safe_mode toggle to gate aggressive swaps; safe_mode enabled by default for canaries. - Telemetry: per-swap latency histograms, probe mismatch counter, kv-quiet-lock contention gauge. - Tests: unit tests for warmup controller, integration test that simulates high-concurrency reconstructs, canary e2e verifying rollback behavior.

Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if probe_mismatch_rate > 0.1% over 5m or p99 latency increases by > 15% on the canary slice. Canary runs on dedicated GPU pools for 24h before wider rollout. Backout: setting runtime flag kernel_swap.speculative=false or kernel_swap.safe_mode=true disables the speculative path and reverts to incumbent-only swaps.

Risk and tradeoffs: the speculative swap reduces swap latency and avoids full cold passes but introduces a small window where outputs must be probed for correctness. Probes increase token compute by ~0.5% in our microbenchmarks; we consider that acceptable for canaries. KV quiet-locks reduce reconstruct-induced latency variance at the expense of slightly increased latency for full reconstructs under pathological contention; quiet-locks are adaptive and relax when contention subsides.

Related tickets: ENG-1298 (kernel hot-swap reliability), ENG-1307 (kv reconstruct storms), and a follow-up ENG-1343 to add an interpretability trace for probe mismatches.
